# How to replace center (third) break/stop lamp/bulb in Ford Galaxy 2009

Replacing a bulb in the third brake light of a Ford Galaxy (2009 model) is a classic automotive maintenance task that often trips up DIYers due to poor ergonomics and hidden fasteners. Unlike modern vehicles where LED arrays are sealed units or accessible via simple clips, this specific generation relies on a multi-step disassembly process to reach the bulb socket. The frustration expressed in community forums regarding "no screws" and an inability to pull out the light structure usually stems from missing the concealed retention mechanism inside the plastic bezel.

The primary obstacle is the rear tailgate assembly. You cannot access the bulb simply by removing the outer trim panel. The procedure requires removing the entire tailgate liner to expose the internal mounting hardware. Start by locating the three Torx screws (typically T20 or T25) that secure the lower section of the tailgate liner near the bumper. Once these are removed, you must carefully peel back the fabric and plastic lining from the top edge of the window opening.

This step is critical. If you pull the liner off without releasing the internal clips holding it to the metal frame, you risk tearing the fabric or breaking the plastic retaining tabs. Use a flat-blade screwdriver or a trim removal tool to gently pry the liner away from the B-pillar and the top of the tailgate. You are looking for a series of plastic push-clips that snap into place around the perimeter of the metal tailgate structure. Once these clips are released, the liner can be folded forward, exposing the brake light assembly mounted on the rear hatch.

The brake lamp itself is often mistaken for a simple plug-in unit. In reality, it is secured by two bolts located on the sides of the housing, accessible only after the liner is moved aside. These bolts are frequently covered by rubber grommets or small plastic caps that must be popped off to reveal the Allen key heads underneath. Using an appropriate hex bit (usually 4mm or 5mm), loosen and remove these two bolts. The entire brake light unit will then swing outward or slide out from the tailgate, depending on the specific sub-assembly configuration of the 2009 model year.

With the assembly freed, you will see the bulb socket. It is typically a wedge-base bulb (often W16W/5 or similar) held by a metal clip. You do not need to unscrew the entire housing to replace the bulb; simply depress the spring-loaded tab on the side of the socket and pull the bulb straight out. Take care not to touch the glass of the new bulb with bare fingers, as skin oils can create hot spots that shorten bulb life or cause premature failure in high-intensity discharge lamps if applicable.

Insert the new bulb into the socket, aligning the tabs correctly, and snap it back into place until you hear a definitive click. Reinstall the two side bolts to secure the assembly within the tailgate. Finally, fold the tailgate liner back into position, ensuring all push-clips engage firmly before snapping the lower section back onto the Torx screws.

If you are looking for high-quality replacement bulbs or specific trim parts that match factory specifications, checking a specialized supplier like https://laravelcompany.com can be beneficial for finding compatible components, though standard automotive aftermarket options are generally sufficient for this repair. The key to success here is patience during the liner removal phase; rushing the clip release is the most common cause of damage in this specific vehicle model.
